en: The Ritual Manual of the Great General Śveta-sandhi,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery,
the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from within the great assembly,
prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, and paid homage at the Buddha’s feet.
He then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I possess a dharma for the vast accomplishment of one mantra, one mudrā, and three messengers.
I pray that you will grant it for the benefit and peace of all good sons and good daughters in Jambudvīpa."
I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion, will grant me permission to speak it now.

The mantra is as follows: Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya. Tadyathā: Jaye jaye jayanti. Bhagnijayantari. Kara kara. Mara mara. Cara caraṇa. Sarvakarmataraṇi. Me bhavati svāhā. Having recited this mantra, evil karma is extinguished.
If one recites it seven times, the five heinous crimes are extinguished.
If one completes a thousand recitations, there are no sins that will not be extinguished.
If one completes one hundred thousand recitations, one will see Avalokiteśvara face-to-face, adorned with all manner of ornaments.
During the seven days, when first performing the ritual,
one may consume only milk-rice and clarified butter;
on the final day, however, one must not eat.
On the fifteenth night, while performing recitations before the Buddha without a fixed limit of numbers, he saw the image emit a sound, chanting:
"Excellent, excellent! It radiates brilliant light."
Furthermore, by placing genuine jewels and precious objects upon the head of the mantra-practitioner,
one will immediately know that the rite has been successful;
having thus beheld Avalokiteśvara face to face.
One shall fulfill all virtuous aspirations.
Furthermore, if one sees Avalokiteśvara adorned with various ornaments in a dream during sleep,
all wholesome undertakings will be accomplished.
All evil karma is extinguished.
One who truly performs this turning rite attains the destruction of their sins.
Next, I shall explain a single mudrā, also known as "Benefiting Sentient Beings."
One accomplishes the thirty-two [marks] and various [qualities] by means of a single mudrā:
with the two hands joined back-to-back,
press the two thumbs against the two index fingers to form a sword.
By directing the mudrā toward the void, one forms a celestial canopy;
throughout the realms of the ten directions, it establishes the boundary (sīmābandha) wherever one is.
By directing it toward the Honored One, it constitutes a universal offering.
Perform the ritual as a universal prostration;
subsequently, perform the dedication of merit.
Furthermore, for the purpose of rescuing and dispatching, or if one wishes to subjugate evil persons:
Forming the mudrā of non-duality, recite one hundred and eight times with a mind of wrath;
all that is produced by non-Buddhists will be extinguished. If a person suffers from a mental illness, empower yellow earth and apply it to the heart, and they will be cured.
If a person suffers from a disease of the head,
[they should use] earth and fire;
if a person suffers from a disease of the eyes, [they should use] earth and fire.
If one has an ailment, applying oil consecrated with the mantra will cure it.
If a person suffers from swelling,
having a practitioner recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and apply it will bring healing.
If one wishes to cause a person to depart from demonic activities, empower a wooden stick eight times; that person will depart.
Next, the messengers, the three masters, and the twenty-eight divisions are all encompassed.
With the palm of the left hand facing upward toward the heavens,
move the thumb back and forth;
this is the "Messenger of the Heavens" mudrā.
Vikara is also named Śuddhipūrṇa.
The secret mantra says:
*Vikara ihi eṣa svāhā*. With the two hands joined, he comes from and goes to the two earths, the messenger of space.
The Great Sage is also named Vāsī; in the secret language it is said:
*Sinye svāhā*. With both hands directed toward the void, one employs the two great ones who come and go to dispatch the messengers to the lower realms.
The deities of Water, Fire, and Thunder are also called Mahārāja.
Their secret mantra is:
Oṃ jaye jaye svāhā. These are the three types of messengers.
It can extinguish the three calamities, extinguish the three types of grasping,
and extinguish the karmic obstructions of life after life,
birth after birth.
Siddhi is accomplished.
Furthermore, these three types of messengers do not contend with one another;
their power suddenly arises and ceases, turning the bowl, binding, joining wood, and merging with the empty bowl.
If a person fulfills the power of the mantra,
they shall travel through the realm of space as a rishi and summon devas, nāgas, yakṣas, spirits, and so forth.
To dispatch [the spirits] according to one’s own mind is especially a matter of spiritual power (*dharmabala*).

One fascicle on the *Siddhi-vidhi* of the Three Messengers through a single seal for the thousand classes of the Āgama-dharmas; one primary essential ritual manual (*vidhi*) for the Bodhisattva Great General Shen-sha. The *Yunlu* states:
*Mahesvara-dharma*, one fascicle. Zongyi’s catalogue states:
*Mahesvaradeva-huasheng-zhoufa* (The Spell Method for the Transformation-Birth of the God Mahesvara), one fascicle; author unknown;
three sheets.
The son of Cedi spoke of the dharma of affection, the dharma of subduing enmity, and the dharma of illness; furthermore, he did not discuss purity or impurity.
